review_comment: Should this be at the warn level?

I don't think so. This code should only execute in one scenario: the migration of a data stream starts -> the [child task](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/8.x/x-pack/plugin/migrate/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/migrate/task/ReindexDataStreamPersistentTaskExecutor.java#L52) migrating the data stream fails for some reason -> the user restarts the system indices migration task.

Since the data stream migration task [retains](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/8.x/x-pack/plugin/migrate/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/migrate/task/ReindexDataStreamPersistentTaskExecutor.java#L295) its status for 1 day, we need to "cancel" the existing task and start a new one to avoid getting the same failure result again. In this case, the failure has already been logged.
"Canceling" the task here is part of normal operation, so I don't think it should be logged as error or warning.  I don't even want to make it info as it might be confusing to see

review_comment:
Could this go into an infinite recursive loop if another part of the system is causing persistent errors? e.g. `migrateDataStream()` -> `checkDataStreamMigrationStatus()` -> `cancelExistingDataStreamMigrationAndRetry()` ->  `cancelDataStreamMigration()` -> `migrateDataStream()` -> ...
(I may be missunderstanding the flow control here)

In the original system index migration logic, an error would just stop the whole migration from continuing, such that a user would need to retry.  I spoke with @gwbrown, who mentioned that this was intentional in case there was a failure elsewhere in the system.  WDYT?

It shouldn't. The chain `migrateDataStream()` -> ... -> `cancelExistingDataStreamMigrationAndRetry()` is possible if a task for migrating that data stream already exists and is in a failed state. In that case, we cancel it and start a new one.
A new task is only started if the cancellation is successful. This means we shouldn't receive a `ResourceAlreadyExistsException` (line 649), which means that `checkDataStreamMigrationStatus` is called with `restartMigrationOnError=false` (line 647).

There is still slight possibility that we end up at the line 714 not because of exception from `dataStreamMigrationFailed` (lines 701 and 703), but because of another error, I will try to improve handling there.

>an error would just stop the whole migration from continuing

Logic here is similar to deleting existing index created during failed migration attempt
